sail.q: You are at the helm, sailing with the wind over your right shoulder and the boom out to the left. Which tack are you on?

figure.note: Wind over the starboard side, boom to port

anchor.q: The anchorage shows 2.4 m on the sounder at low water. The boat's draft is 1.9 m. Can you stay?

rope.q: You need to put a loop in the end of a mooring line to drop over a bollard. Which knot?

figure.note: Loop in the end of a line

encounter.q: A crew member goes over the side on a broad reach. What is the very first thing you shout and do?

dayshape.q: Under sail you meet a vessel with these shapes, towing nets. Who gives way?

figure.note: Two cones apexes together: vessel engaged in fishing

lights.q: Motoring at night you see these lights on a steady bearing, closing. What vessel is it and what do you do?

buoy.q: Entering a Mediterranean harbour from seaward you see this buoy. Which side do you leave it on?

bay.q: A hot sunny morning, calm. By 14:00 a steady 15-knot onshore wind has set in. What is it?

card.q: You fill in the crew list at the desk and the manager asks whether anyone else will sleep aboard this week. What do you say?

figure.title: Crew list
lines: A friend joins Wednesday in Lefkas
Two crew fly home on Thursday
Port police may check at any harbour

panel.q: The technician has already filled in the engine hours on the check-in form. You look at the panel. What do you do?

race.q: Wednesday evening club race, J/24s on a starboard-tack reach. Red is directly behind you; her bow is about a metre behind the line abeam of your transom. In the words of the rules, are you overlapped?

figure.note: Red's bow is 1 m behind the line abeam your transom

chart.q: You need this buoy's position for your waypoint list. What do you write down?

figure.note: Parallels and meridians from the border

compass.q: You have laid off the course to the next waypoint on the chart. The boat has no deviation on this heading. What course do you give the helmsman?

isobars.q: You leave Honolulu for San Francisco in July. The NE trade blows straight down the great circle (054°T, 2,078 M) and the Pacific High lies across its middle. How do you route?

figure.note: GC: on the wind, then calms
